questions.question: How does a Cisco Unified Wireless Network respond to Wi-Fi channel overlap?

options.text: It allows the administrator to assign the channels on a per-device or per-interface basis.
It segregates devices from different manufactures onto different channels.
It analyzes client load and background noise and dynamically assigns a channel.
It alternates automatically between 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz on adjacent access points.

questions.explanation: Wireless radio resource management can monitor interference, noise, and channel utilization and adjust channel assignments.

optionExplanations.A: Manual channel assignment is possible but does not describe the automatic response.
optionExplanations.B: The system does not assign channels based on AP manufacturer.
optionExplanations.C: Wireless radio resource management can monitor interference, noise, and channel utilization and adjust channel assignments.
optionExplanations.D: Alternating frequency bands is not the specified dynamic channel assignment mechanism.

questions.question: In which situation is private IPv4 addressing appropriate for a new subnet on the network of an organization?

options.text: The network has multiple endpoint listeners, and it is desired to limit the number of broadcasts.
The ISP requires the new subnet to be advertised to the Internet for web services.
There is limited unique address space, and traffic on the new subnet will stay local within the organization.
Traffic on the subnet must traverse a site-to-site VPN to an outside organization.

questions.explanation: Private IPv4 addresses are useful for internal networks when globally unique public addresses are not required.

optionExplanations.A: Broadcast reduction is a subnet design question, not a reason to choose private addressing.
optionExplanations.B: Internet-advertised addresses generally require globally routable addressing or translation/proxy.
optionExplanations.C: Private IPv4 addresses are useful for internal networks when globally unique public addresses are not required.
optionExplanations.D: VPN connectivity can use private addressing, but address coordination and overlap still matter.

questions.question: Which 802.11 frame type is indicated by a probe response after a client sends a probe request?
questions.explanation: Probe request and probe response are IEEE 802.11 management frames used during wireless network discovery.

optionExplanations.A: Data frames carry user traffic rather than discovery probe messages.
optionExplanations.B: Probe request and probe response are IEEE 802.11 management frames used during wireless network discovery.
optionExplanations.C: Control frames assist medium access and acknowledgments, not probing.
optionExplanations.D: Action is a management-frame subtype, not the broad frame type being requested.

questions.question: What is the maximum bandwidth of a T1 point-to-point connection?
questions.explanation: A North American T1 circuit has a nominal line rate of 1.544 Mbps (24 DS0 channels plus framing).

optionExplanations.A: A North American T1 circuit has a nominal line rate of 1.544 Mbps (24 DS0 channels plus framing).
optionExplanations.B: 2.048 Mbps is an E1 rate.
optionExplanations.C: 34.368 Mbps is an E3 rate.
optionExplanations.D: 43.7 Mbps is not the nominal T1 rate.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of cloud-based network topology?

options.text: onsite network services are provided with physical Layer 2 and Layer 3 components
wireless connections provide the sole access method to services
physical workstations are configured to share resources
services are provided by a public, private, or hybrid deployment

questions.explanation: Cloud services can be deployed through public, private, or hybrid cloud models; these describe where resources are hosted and managed.

optionExplanations.A: On-site physical networking describes traditional infrastructure, not the defining cloud deployment model.
optionExplanations.B: Cloud services do not require wireless-only access.
optionExplanations.C: Peer resource sharing among physical workstations is not the definition of cloud topology.
optionExplanations.D: Cloud services can be deployed through public, private, or hybrid cloud models; these describe where resources are hosted and managed.

questions.question: Which network action occurs within the data plane?

options.text: reply to an incoming ICMP echo request
make a configuration change from an incoming NETCONF RPC
run routing protocols (OSPF, EIGRP, RIP, BGP)
compare the destination IP address to the IP routing table

questions.explanation: The forwarding/data plane looks up a packet destination in forwarding information derived from routing decisions to choose an egress path.

optionExplanations.A: An ICMP echo reply generated by the router is control-plane processing.
optionExplanations.B: NETCONF configuration belongs to the management plane.
optionExplanations.C: Routing protocols build reachability information in the control plane.
optionExplanations.D: The forwarding/data plane looks up a packet destination in forwarding information derived from routing decisions to choose an egress path.

questions.question: What are network endpoints?

options.text: a threat to the network if they are compromised
act as routers to connect a user to the service provider network
enforce policies for campus-wide traffic going to the Internet

questions.explanation: Endpoints are end-user or workload devices that connect to a network. A compromised endpoint can become an entry point for attacks.

optionExplanations.A: Inter-VLAN routing is performed by Layer 3 infrastructure, not endpoints.
optionExplanations.B: Endpoints are end-user or workload devices that connect to a network. A compromised endpoint can become an entry point for attacks.
optionExplanations.C: Endpoints are not necessarily routers to an ISP.
optionExplanations.D: Campus Internet policy enforcement is a network security infrastructure role.

questions.question: Why was the RFC 1918 address space defined?

options.text: reduce instances of overlapping IP addresses

questions.explanation: RFC 1918 reserves reusable private IPv4 address blocks to reduce demand for globally unique public IPv4 addresses.

optionExplanations.A: RFC 1918 reserves reusable private IPv4 address blocks to reduce demand for globally unique public IPv4 addresses.
optionExplanations.B: RFC 1918 predates and is not solely intended to support NAT.
optionExplanations.C: It defines IPv4 private ranges, not IPv6 address space.
optionExplanations.D: Reusing private ranges can increase, not eliminate, overlapping-address scenarios.

questions.question: Which type of organization should use a collapsed-core architecture?

options.text: small and needs to reduce networking costs
large and must minimize downtime when hardware fails
large and requires a flexible, scalable network design
currently small but is expected to grow dramatically in the near future

questions.explanation: A collapsed-core architecture combines core and distribution functions, reducing equipment and operational complexity for smaller organizations.

optionExplanations.A: A collapsed-core architecture combines core and distribution functions, reducing equipment and operational complexity for smaller organizations.
optionExplanations.B: Large fault-tolerant networks typically benefit from distinct scalable layers.
optionExplanations.C: Large scalable designs generally retain dedicated core/distribution functions.
optionExplanations.D: Expected dramatic growth can justify a more scalable design than a collapsed core.

questions.question:
A network administrator is setting up a new IPv6 network using the 64-bit address 2001:0EB8:00C1:2200:0001:0000:0000:0331/64. To simplify
the configuration, the administrator has decided to compress the address. Which IP address must the administrator configure?
questions.explanation: Compress the IPv6 address by removing leading zeroes from each hextet and replacing the two consecutive all-zero hextets with ::. The 2200 hextet must remain unchanged.

optionExplanations.A: 22 is not 2200; dropping the two trailing zeroes changes that hextet.
optionExplanations.B: 21 is not 2001, so the first hextet is changed.
optionExplanations.C: Only seven hextets are written and the intended zero run is not accurately preserved.

questions.question: What is a similarity between 1000BASE-LX and 1000BASE-T standards?

options.text: Both use the same data-link header and trailer formats.
Both cable types support RJ-45 connectors.
Both support up to 550 meters between nodes.
Both cable types support LR connectors.

questions.explanation: 1000BASE-LX and 1000BASE-T use different physical media but carry Ethernet frames with the same fundamental MAC header and FCS trailer format.

optionExplanations.A: Both are Gigabit Ethernet PHYs using the Ethernet data-link framing format.
optionExplanations.B: 1000BASE-T uses twisted-pair copper with RJ-45; 1000BASE-LX is an optical-fiber specification.
optionExplanations.C: 1000BASE-T normally reaches 100 m on supported copper cabling, not 550 m.
optionExplanations.D: An LR-style optical connector is not used by the RJ-45 copper 1000BASE-T physical interface.

questions.domainTopic: Network Fundamentals / Cabling and physical interfaces

questions.question: Which function forwards frames to ports that have a matching destination MAC address?
questions.explanation: A switch uses its MAC address table to choose the egress port for a known destination; this is normal unicast frame switching.

optionExplanations.A: Flooding sends an unknown-unicast frame out multiple eligible ports, not to a specifically learned destination port.
optionExplanations.B: Filtering suppresses forwarding on a port, such as when the learned destination is on the ingress port.
optionExplanations.C: Frame pushing is not the standard Ethernet forwarding function described here.
optionExplanations.D: Frame switching uses the learned destination MAC-to-port association to forward a frame on the appropriate egress interface.

questions.question: Which type of IPv6 address is similar to a unicast address but is assigned to multiple devices on the same network at the same time?
questions.explanation: An IPv6 anycast address is assigned to multiple interfaces, with a packet delivered to one reachable instance, typically the nearest by routing metric.

optionExplanations.A: Global unicast identifies a particular interface, rather than a group of equivalent destinations.
optionExplanations.B: Link-local is a scope of unicast addressing, normally confined to one link.
optionExplanations.C: Anycast reuses a unicast-form address on more than one interface and routes to one instance.
optionExplanations.D: Multicast delivers to members of a multicast group, potentially multiple receivers, not one selected instance.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of private IPv4 addressing?

options.text: composed of up to 65,536 available addresses
issued by IANA in conjunction with an autonomous system number
traverse the Internet when an outbound ACL is applied

questions.explanation: Private IPv4 address ranges can be used inside organizations without external allocation or global registration, subject to local coordination.

optionExplanations.A: The RFC 1918 spaces collectively contain far more than 65,536 IPv4 addresses.
optionExplanations.B: RFC 1918 private addresses are not issued with an AS number to individual organizations.
optionExplanations.C: Private addresses require no global registration, though administrators should coordinate internally.
optionExplanations.D: An outbound ACL does not make RFC 1918 addresses globally routable.

questions.question: What is a function of an endpoint on a network?

options.text: provides wireless services to users in a building
connects server and client device to a network
allows users to record data and transmit to a file server
forwards traffic between VLANs on a network

questions.explanation: Endpoints are hosts such as PCs or phones that generate or consume user/application data; they can create files and send them to servers.

optionExplanations.A: Providing building-wide wireless service describes an access point or WLAN infrastructure role.
optionExplanations.B: Connecting client and server devices to a LAN as a networking function describes a switch or access port.
optionExplanations.C: Recording user data and sending it to a file server is a typical endpoint activity.
optionExplanations.D: Forwarding between VLANs is a router or Layer 3 switch function.

questions.question: What is the function of a controller in controller-based networking?

options.text: It serves as the centralized management point of an SDN architecture
It is a pair of core routers that maintain all routing decisions for a campus
It centralizes the data plane for the network
It is the card on a core router that maintains all routing decisions for a campus.

questions.explanation: A controller offers centralized network control, policy, and management in controller-based/SDN architectures; forwarding remains distributed on network devices.

optionExplanations.A: A software-defined controller coordinates and manages network behavior centrally.
optionExplanations.B: A fixed pair of core routers is not the definition of an SDN controller.
optionExplanations.C: The SDN design does not require centralizing packet forwarding in the controller.
optionExplanations.D: A controller is not merely a routing card inside a campus core router.

questions.question: How do TCP and UDP fit into a query-responsible model?

options.text: TCP avoids using sequencing and UDP avoids using acknowledgments
TCP establishes a connection prior to sending data, and UDP sends immediately
TCP encourages out-of-order packet delivery, and UDP prevents re-ordering
TCP uses error detection for packets, and UDP uses error recovery.

questions.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented and normally establishes a session with a three-way handshake; UDP is connectionless and has no comparable setup handshake.

optionExplanations.A: TCP uses sequence numbers; the statement wrongly claims it avoids sequencing.
optionExplanations.B: TCP establishes a connection before application data, while UDP can transmit datagrams without such setup.
optionExplanations.C: TCP provides in-order byte-stream delivery; UDP does not guarantee in-order delivery.
optionExplanations.D: Both TCP and UDP use checksums for error detection; UDP does not provide TCP-style retransmission recovery.

questions.question: What provides centralized control of authentication and roaming in an enterprise network?
questions.explanation: A wireless LAN controller centrally manages lightweight access points, WLAN security/authentication integration, and mobility/roaming functions.

optionExplanations.A: A lightweight AP handles radio communication but usually relies on a controller for centralized coordination.
optionExplanations.B: The WLC coordinates multiple APs and supports centralized WLAN authentication and roaming policies.
optionExplanations.C: A firewall primarily filters traffic; it is not the central controller for WLAN roaming.
optionExplanations.D: An Ethernet switch provides wired connectivity, not central wireless mobility management.

questions.question: Which set of 2 4 GHz nonoverlapping wireless channels is standard in the United States?
questions.explanation: In conventional 20/22-MHz 2.4-GHz Wi-Fi channel plans in the United States, channels 1, 6, and 11 are the standard nonoverlapping set.

optionExplanations.A: Channel 14 is not permitted for ordinary 2.4-GHz Wi-Fi operation in the United States.
optionExplanations.B: Channels 7 and 9 overlap with each other, so the set is unsuitable.
optionExplanations.C: The frequencies used by channels 2 and 7 overlap substantially with nearby channels in the proposed set.
optionExplanations.D: Channels 1, 6, and 11 are sufficiently separated for nonoverlapping 20/22-MHz channel use.

questions.question:
A network engineer is installing an IPv6-only capable device. The client has requested that the device IP address be reachable only from the
internal network.
Which type of IPv6 address must the engineer assign?
questions.explanation: Unique local addresses (typically FD00::/8 in locally assigned deployments) support internally routed IPv6 communication without global Internet advertisement. A link-local address is restricted to one link.

optionExplanations.A: IPv4-compatible IPv6 addresses are an obsolete transition form, not the appropriate internal IPv6 scope.
optionExplanations.B: Unique local addresses are intended for communication within a site or cooperating sites, not global Internet routing.
optionExplanations.C: A link-local address is confined to one Layer 2 link and is not appropriate if the internal network includes multiple routed subnets.
optionExplanations.D: Global IPv6 unicast addresses are globally routable by design, unlike the private scope requested.

questions.question: What is a requirement for nonoverlapping Wi-Fi channels?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi channels are nonoverlapping when their occupied spectral ranges do not materially overlap at the selected channel width.

optionExplanations.A: Security settings have no effect on the RF frequency ranges occupied by Wi-Fi channels.
optionExplanations.B: Discontinuous/separated occupied frequency ranges are necessary for nonoverlapping channels.
optionExplanations.C: SSIDs are network identifiers and do not determine RF spectral overlap.
optionExplanations.D: Data rate is not the property that determines whether two channels overlap spectrally.

questions.question:
A network engineer must implement an IPv6 configuration on the vlan 2000 interface to create a routable locally-unique unicast address that is
blocked from being advertised to the internet. Which configuration must the engineer apply?
questions.explanation: The fd00::/8 locally assigned ULA range is appropriate for IPv6 addresses routed within private networks rather than advertised on the public Internet.

optionExplanations.A: FF00::/8 is multicast address space, not an IPv6 unicast interface address.
optionExplanations.B: FD00::/8 represents locally assigned ULAs; in a real deployment use an appropriately generated unique ULA /48 prefix.
optionExplanations.C: FE80::/10 addresses are link-local and cannot be routed between internal IPv6 subnets.
optionExplanations.D: FC00::/8 has the ULA local (L) bit cleared, for which RFC 4193 does not define a local allocation procedure; it is not the suitable locally assigned choice.

questions.question: When a switch receives a frame for a known destination MAC address, how is the frame handled?

options.text: flooded to all ports except the one from which it originated
forwarded to the first available port
sent to the port identified for the known MAC address

questions.explanation: For a known unicast destination, the switch looks up the learned destination MAC and forwards on the associated port, assuming it is eligible for forwarding.

optionExplanations.A: Flooding is the normal behavior for unknown unicast, broadcast, or certain multicast traffic, not a known unicast.
optionExplanations.B: The switch uses the destination MAC table entry rather than the first available port.
optionExplanations.C: A known unicast is directed to its learned egress port.
optionExplanations.D: Broadcasting to all ports is not how a known unicast destination is normally handled.

questions.question: What is the collapsed layer in collapsed core architectures?
questions.explanation: Collapsed-core campus architecture combines the distribution and core functions into a shared tier, leaving a simplified two-tier design.

optionExplanations.A: The core and distribution tiers are combined in the collapsed-core design.
optionExplanations.B: An access/WAN tier is not the collapsed layer.
optionExplanations.C: The access tier remains distinct from the combined core/distribution tier.
optionExplanations.D: WAN and core are not the standard pair collapsed together.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a SOHO network?

options.text: includes at least three tiers of devices to provide load balancing and redundancy
connects each switch to every other switch in the network
enables multiple users to share a single broadband connection
provides high throughput access for 1000 or more users

questions.explanation: A small-office/home-office network commonly shares a broadband Internet uplink among multiple local users.

optionExplanations.A: Three-tier redundant campus architecture is not a defining requirement for a SOHO.
optionExplanations.B: A full-mesh of switches is not required and is rarely a sensible small-network topology.
optionExplanations.C: Sharing one broadband connection via a router or gateway is typical SOHO functionality.
optionExplanations.D: Supporting 1,000 or more users describes a much larger network than a typical SOHO.

questions.question: What is the role of disaggregation in controller-based networking?

options.text: It divides the control-plane and data-plane functions.
It streamlines traffic handling by assigning individual devices to perform either Layer 2 or Layer 3 functions
It summarizes the routes between the core and distribution layers of the network topology
It enables a network topology to quickly adjust from a ring network to a star network

questions.explanation: Disaggregation separates control-plane decision logic from data-plane forwarding; it can enable centralized controller-based management.

optionExplanations.A: Control-plane and data-plane functions are separated rather than tightly bundled in every device.
optionExplanations.B: Separating L2 switches from L3 routers is not the meaning of control/data disaggregation.
optionExplanations.C: Route summarization is an IP-routing optimization unrelated to the SDN architectural split.
optionExplanations.D: Reconfiguring a physical ring into a star is not what network disaggregation means.

questions.question: What is a function performed by a web server?

options.text: send and retrieve email from client devices
securely store files for FTP access
authenticate and authorize a user's identity
provide an application that is transmitted over HTTP

questions.explanation: Web servers host or deliver HTTP-based resources and applications to web clients.

optionExplanations.A: Sending/retrieving user email is an SMTP/IMAP/POP service role, not a basic web-server function.
optionExplanations.B: Providing an FTP file store describes an FTP server; web servers ordinarily use HTTP/HTTPS.
optionExplanations.C: Authentication can be integrated with web applications, but identity authorization alone does not define a web server.
optionExplanations.D: Delivering websites or web applications through HTTP is the core web-server function.

questions.question: Which PoE mode enables powered-devices detection and guarantees power when the device detected?
questions.explanation: Cisco PoE static mode detects powered devices but pre-reserves power even before detection; therefore available power is guaranteed when the device appears.

optionExplanations.A: Auto discovers powered devices and allocates power only if the remaining budget allows; it does not reserve guaranteed capacity.
optionExplanations.B: Static power mode preallocates the power budget and guarantees it on powered-device detection.
optionExplanations.C: Dynamic is not the Cisco power inline mode that provides this reserved-power guarantee.
optionExplanations.D: Active is not the relevant Cisco power inline mode documented for guaranteed allocation.

questions.question: How is RFC 1918 addressing used in a network?

options.text: They are used to access the Internet from the internal network without conversion.
They are used in place of public addresses for Increased security.
They are used with NAT to preserve public IPv4 addresses.
They are used by Internet Service Providers to route over the Internet.

questions.explanation: RFC 1918 permits reusing private IPv4 address space; NAT/PAT commonly lets many private hosts share fewer public IPv4 addresses.

optionExplanations.A: RFC 1918 source addresses are not generally routed on the global Internet without translation or encapsulation.
optionExplanations.B: Private addressing can reduce direct inbound exposure, but it is not itself a comprehensive security control.
optionExplanations.C: NAT with private addresses conserves public IPv4 space by translating internal traffic as required.
optionExplanations.D: The public Internet does not route RFC 1918 destinations as normal globally unique space.

questions.domainTopic: IP Services / NAT and private addressing

questions.question: Which WAN topology has the highest degree of reliability?
questions.explanation: Full-mesh WANs provide multiple alternate paths between sites and remove dependence on a single central hub, at increased cost and complexity.

optionExplanations.A: A single point-to-point connection has no alternative path unless redundant parallel links are provided.
optionExplanations.B: Router-on-a-stick is a method for inter-VLAN routing, not a WAN topology.
optionExplanations.C: Full mesh gives every site a direct connection to all others and offers maximum topology redundancy among these choices.
optionExplanations.D: Hub-and-spoke depends on the hub and offers fewer alternate site-to-site paths.

questions.question: What causes a port to be placed in the err-disabled state?

options.text: shutdown command issued on the port

questions.explanation: Cisco switches can place a port in err-disabled state after repeated link flapping if the relevant detection is enabled and the platform thresholds are crossed.

optionExplanations.A: A disconnected port ordinarily just shows a down/notconnect state; the absence of a cable is not by itself err-disable.
optionExplanations.B: Rapid repeated link-up/link-down events may trip link-flap err-disable protection.
optionExplanations.C: Latency is a performance metric and not itself a direct cause of err-disable.
optionExplanations.D: An administratively shutdown interface is administratively down, not automatically err-disabled.

questions.question:
A network engineer must configure an interface with IP address 10.10.10.145 and a subnet mask equivalent to
11111111.11111111.11111111.11111000. Which subnet mask must the engineer use?
questions.explanation: 11111000 is 248, which has five leading 1 bits in the last octet; 24 + 5 = /29. The corresponding dotted mask is 255.255.255.248.

optionExplanations.A: /29 equals 255.255.255.248 and matches the supplied binary mask.
optionExplanations.C: /27 ends in 11100000 (224), which has only three last-octet mask bits set.
optionExplanations.D: /28 ends in 11110000 (240), rather than the specified 11111000.

questions.question: Which property is shared by 10GBase-SR and 10GBase-LR interfaces?

options.text: Both use the single-mode fiber type.
Both require UTP cable media for transmission.
Both require fiber cable media for transmission.
Both use the multimode fiber type.

questions.explanation: 10GBASE-SR and 10GBASE-LR are both 10-Gigabit Ethernet optical PHYs; SR typically uses multimode fiber, whereas LR uses single-mode fiber.

optionExplanations.A: SR generally operates on multimode, not the single-mode fiber used by LR.
optionExplanations.B: Neither standard relies on UTP copper as its stated transmission medium.
optionExplanations.C: Both use fiber-optic cabling, even though their usual fiber types and reach differ.
optionExplanations.D: LR uses single-mode rather than multimode fiber for its normal specified application.

questions.question: Which device permits or denies network traffic based on a set of rules?
questions.explanation: A firewall applies policy rules to permit, deny, and often inspect network traffic between security zones.

optionExplanations.A: A conventional switch primarily forwards Layer 2 frames; it is not the device defined by security policy enforcement.
optionExplanations.B: A firewall is designed to evaluate traffic against access-control and security policy rules.
optionExplanations.C: A WLC manages wireless networks and APs rather than serving primarily as a network firewall.
optionExplanations.D: An AP supplies wireless connectivity, not general-purpose perimeter traffic filtering.

questions.question: What is the role of a firewall in an enterprise network?

options.text: determines which packets are allowed to cross from unsecured to secured networks
processes unauthorized packets and allows passage to less secure segments of the network
forwards packets based on stateless packet inspection
explicitly denies all packets from entering an administrative domain

questions.explanation: Firewalls enforce security policy between trust zones, such as permitting approved inbound or outbound traffic while blocking unauthorized traffic.

optionExplanations.A: A firewall evaluates whether traffic is allowed to cross security boundaries according to configured rules.
optionExplanations.B: A firewall is intended to stop unauthorized traffic rather than process it and then permit it toward less-secure segments.
optionExplanations.C: Many firewalls are stateful; claiming all such forwarding is stateless inspection misdescribes typical enterprise firewalls.
optionExplanations.D: Firewalls are policy configurable and do not universally deny every packet entering an administrative domain.

questions.question: What is a function spine-and-leaf architecture?

options.text: Offers predictable latency of the traffic path between end devices.
Exclusively sends multicast traffic between servers that are directly connected to the spine.
Mitigates oversubscription by adding a layer of leaf switches.
Limits payload size of traffic within the leaf layer.

questions.explanation: In spine-leaf designs, traffic traveling between hosts on different leaves generally traverses leaf–spine–leaf, giving a predictable hop count and latency.

optionExplanations.A: The regular leaf-to-spine-to-leaf path makes inter-leaf hop count comparatively predictable.
optionExplanations.B: Spine-leaf architectures carry various traffic types; not only multicast traffic between directly connected servers.
optionExplanations.C: Adding a leaf tier does not by itself guarantee that oversubscription is eliminated.
optionExplanations.D: Spine-leaf does not inherently impose a smaller payload size specifically in the leaf tier.

questions.question: What is the function of the control plane?

options.text: It provides CLI access to the network device.
It looks up an egress interface in the forwarding information base.
It forwards traffic to the next hop.

questions.explanation: The control plane establishes reachability and routing state by exchanging routing information; forwarding individual packets is a data-plane activity.

optionExplanations.A: Routing protocols exchange reachability/routing information in the control plane.
optionExplanations.B: CLI administration is a management-plane function.
optionExplanations.C: FIB lookup used to select an egress interface is executed as a data-plane operation.
optionExplanations.D: Actual forwarding of transit traffic to the next hop belongs to the data plane.

questions.question: What is a benefit for external users who consume public cloud resources?

options.text: Located in the same data center as the users

questions.explanation: Public-cloud services are typically delivered to customers over Internet-accessible interfaces rather than requiring users to be in the same building or data center.

optionExplanations.A: Public cloud does not require a customer-owned dedicated WAN; private connectivity is an optional access method.
optionExplanations.B: Although hardware underlies cloud services, calling every service physically hosted describes neither the user benefit nor the access model.
optionExplanations.C: Internet accessibility is a defining access benefit of public cloud resources.
optionExplanations.D: Public cloud resources are normally operated in remote provider data centers, not colocated with the user.

questions.question:
An engineer must update the configuration on two PCs in two different subnets to communicate locally with each other. One PC is configured with
IP address
192.168.25.128/25 and the other with 192.168.25.100/25. Which network mask must the engineer configure on both PCs to enable the
communication?
questions.explanation: A /24 mask puts 192.168.25.100 and 192.168.25.128 in the same IPv4 subnet. With /25, .128 is the second subnet network address rather than a usable host address.

optionExplanations.A: /29 produces small subnets and does not place .100 and .128 in the same local network.
optionExplanations.C: /24 covers 192.168.25.0–192.168.25.255 and treats both .100 and .128 as usable host addresses.
optionExplanations.D: /30 makes still-smaller different networks and cannot satisfy the requirement.

questions.question: Which key function is provided by the data plane?

options.text: Forwarding traffic to the next hop

questions.explanation: The data plane forwards packets by performing per-packet forwarding-table lookups and transmitting toward the selected next hop.

optionExplanations.A: Endpoints or the device itself originate packets, but packet origination is not the defining transit data-plane function.
optionExplanations.B: Exchanging routing protocol information belongs to the control plane.
optionExplanations.C: Computing routing choices and building routing state is associated with the control plane, not the per-packet forwarding task.
optionExplanations.D: Sending transit traffic toward its next hop is the characteristic data-plane responsibility.

questions.question: When should an engineer implement a collapsed-core architecture?

options.text: For small networks with minimal need for growth
For large networks that are connected to multiple remote sites
The access and distribution layers must be on the same device

questions.explanation: A collapsed-core campus design combines core and distribution functions, which is usually cost-effective for smaller relatively stable networks.

optionExplanations.A: Virtual Switching System can be used in some designs but is not a prerequisite for the architecture.
optionExplanations.B: A smaller network with limited near-term growth is the strongest fit for a combined core/distribution tier.
optionExplanations.C: Large multisite networks often require independent and scalable distribution/core capabilities.
optionExplanations.D: Combining access and distribution is not the standard definition of collapsed core; it combines core with distribution.

questions.question: What is the difference between 1000BASE-LX/LH and 1000BASE-ZX interfaces?

options.text: 1000BASE-LX/LH interoperates with multimode and single-mode fiber, and 1000BASE-ZX needs a conditioning patch cable with multimode.
1000BASE-ZX interoperates with dual-rate 100M/1G 10Km SFP over multimode fiber, and 1000BASE-LX/LH supports only single-rate
1000BASE-ZX is supported on links up to 1000km, and 1000BASE-LX/LH operates over links up to 70 km
1000BASE- LX/LH is supported on links up to 10km, and 1000Base-ZX operates over links up to 70 km

questions.explanation: Cisco 1000BASE-LX/LH optics typically reach up to about 10 km over single-mode fiber, while 1000BASE-ZX products support about 70 km under normal link-budget assumptions.

optionExplanations.A: The statement about ZX needing multimode conditioning is wrong; ZX is designed for long-reach single-mode fiber.
optionExplanations.B: The quoted dual-rate multimode ZX capability is not the defining ZX/LX difference.
optionExplanations.C: The reach numbers are reversed and the 1,000 km ZX claim is incorrect.
optionExplanations.D: 10 km for Cisco LX/LH and roughly 70 km for ZX is the standard product-family comparison.

questions.question: Which concern is addressed with the use of private IPv4 addressing?

options.text: Lack of routing protocol support for CIDR and VLSM
Lack of security protocols at the network perimeter
Lack of available TCP/UDP ports per IPv5 address
Lack of available publicly routable unique IPv4 address

questions.explanation: RFC 1918 private addressing permits multiple organizations to reuse internal IPv4 space, conserving scarce globally unique public IPv4 addresses.

optionExplanations.A: CIDR and VLSM are supported by classless routing protocols; private addresses do not solve protocol incompatibility.
optionExplanations.B: Private addresses are not a security perimeter; access control and firewalls are independent requirements.
optionExplanations.C: IPv5 is not the normal operational internet protocol here; port-number exhaustion is not the primary motivation for RFC 1918 addressing.
optionExplanations.D: Public IPv4 exhaustion motivates the reuse of private IPv4 address ranges inside separate networks.

questions.question: What is the difference between IPv6 unicast and anycast addressing?

options.text:
An individual IPv6 unicast address is supported on a single interface on one node, but an IPv6 anycast address is assigned to a group of
interfaces on multiple nodes.
IPv6 anycast nodes must be explicitly configured to recognize the anycast address, but IPv6 unicast nodes require no special configuration.
IPv6 unicast nodes must be explicitly configured to recognize the unicast address, but IPv6 anycast nodes require no special configuration.
Unlike an IPv6 anycast address, an IPv6 unicast address is assigned to a group of interfaces on multiple nodes.

questions.explanation: RFC 4291 defines unicast as identifying one interface and anycast as identifying a set of interfaces; routing delivers an anycast packet to one of the members.

optionExplanations.A: Unicast is directed to one interface; anycast can be assigned to different nodes and routed toward one member.
optionExplanations.B: While anycast requires correct configuration, this is not the defining contrast and unicast must also be configured.
optionExplanations.C: The configuration requirement is reversed and does not capture address delivery semantics.
optionExplanations.D: This describes anycast, not ordinary unicast.

questions.question: How are the switches in a spine-and-leaf topology interconnected?

options.text: Each leaf switch is connected to one of the spine switches
Each leaf switch is connected to each spine switch.
Each leaf switch is connected to two spine switches, making a loop.
Each leaf switch is connected to a central leaf switch, then uplinked to a core spine switch.

questions.explanation: In a conventional leaf–spine fabric every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, providing consistent hop count and ECMP paths.

optionExplanations.A: Connecting each leaf to only one spine eliminates the usual redundant paths across the spine layer.
optionExplanations.B: Full leaf-to-spine connectivity is the defining leaf–spine design pattern.
optionExplanations.C: Using exactly two spines is a possible deployment but not a requirement or the definition; links to both spines do not inherently create a Layer 2 loop.
optionExplanations.D: Leaves are not chained through a central leaf; they uplink to spine switches.

questions.question: What is the primary effect of the spanning-tree portfast command?

options.text: It immediately enables the port in the listening state.
It immediately puts the port into the forwarding state when the switch is reloaded.

questions.explanation: PortFast shortens host-facing access to forwarding by bypassing the classic STP listening and learning delay.

optionExplanations.A: PortFast does not place the port into listening; it skips listening and learning.
optionExplanations.B: PortFast may enable rapid forwarding on link-up but the statement is over-specific about switch reload, and standard STP behavior may apply during startup.
optionExplanations.C: BPDU reception is not enabled by PortFast; BPDU processing is separate.
optionExplanations.D: Eliminating the usual startup delay reduces time to forwarding on a host-facing port.

questions.question: Which QoS Profile is selected in the GUI when configuring a voice over WLAN deployment?
questions.explanation: Cisco AireOS Wireless LAN Controllers classify VoIP/WLAN voice traffic as Platinum QoS, above Gold (video), Silver (best effort), and Bronze (background).

optionExplanations.A: Platinum is the controller QoS class intended for latency-sensitive voice communications.
optionExplanations.B: Bronze is the low-priority/background or guest class, not the recommended voice class.
optionExplanations.C: Gold is normally video priority, below Platinum voice.
optionExplanations.D: Silver is the default best-effort traffic class, not the VoIP profile.

questions.question: Which unified access point mode continues to serve wireless clients after losing connectivity to the Cisco Wireless LAN Controller?
questions.explanation: FlexConnect access points can switch configured WLAN user traffic locally when controller connectivity is interrupted, subject to configuration and authentication limitations.

optionExplanations.A: Local-mode APs rely on WLC CAPWAP for ordinary client forwarding and generally cannot continue full standalone service on controller loss.
optionExplanations.B: Mesh mode addresses wireless backhaul and does not by itself provide the required disconnected local switching behavior.
optionExplanations.C: FlexConnect supports local switching at the branch and continued service for eligible locally switched WLANs.
optionExplanations.D: Sniffer mode is used to capture RF frames; it does not serve clients as a normal AP.

questions.question: Which mode must be used to configure EtherChannel between two switches without using a negotiation protocol?
questions.explanation: Static EtherChannel mode `on` forces aggregation without LACP or PAgP negotiation, requiring consistent configuration at both ends.

optionExplanations.A: Active is an LACP mode that sends negotiation PDUs.
optionExplanations.B: On is the static mode that does not negotiate.
optionExplanations.C: Auto is a passive PAgP mode; it expects PAgP negotiation.
optionExplanations.D: Desirable is an active PAgP mode and initiates negotiation.

questions.question: Which mode allows access points to be managed by Cisco Wireless LAN Controllers?
questions.explanation: A lightweight AP joins and is centrally managed by a compatible wireless LAN controller, unlike autonomous standalone APs.

optionExplanations.A: Bridge is an AP connectivity role/mode, not the general mode defining controller management.
optionExplanations.B: Lightweight APs use a controller-based control protocol, normally CAPWAP, for centralized management.
optionExplanations.C: Mobility Express is a controller capability hosted on selected AP platforms, not the generic lightweight AP mode.
optionExplanations.D: Autonomous APs manage their own configuration rather than depending on a central WLC.

questions.question: Which command is used to specify the delay time in seconds for LLDP to initialize on any interface?
questions.explanation: `lldp reinit` configures the LLDP transmitter reinitialization delay in seconds rather than its send timer or hold time.

optionExplanations.A: `lldp timer` controls the periodic advertisement interval, not the reinitialization delay.
optionExplanations.B: `lldp tlv-select` controls the information elements advertised.
optionExplanations.C: `lldp reinit` controls how long LLDP waits before restarting transmission after a state change.
optionExplanations.D: `lldp holdtime` controls how long advertised neighbor information remains valid.

questions.question:
Two switches are connected and using Cisco Dynamic Trunking Protocol. SW1 is set to Dynamic Auto and SW2 is set to Dynamic Desirable. What
is the result of this configuration?

options.text: The link becomes an access port.
The link is in an error disabled state.
The link is in a down state.
The link becomes a trunk port.

questions.explanation: DTP dynamic desirable actively negotiates trunking, while dynamic auto is willing to become a trunk. The combination forms a trunk on compatible Cisco switches.

optionExplanations.A: An access link would result when DTP fails to negotiate, such as auto plus auto, not desirable plus auto.
optionExplanations.B: DTP desirable/auto does not inherently put the port in errdisable.
optionExplanations.C: There is no reason for the link to go down solely because of these compatible DTP modes.
optionExplanations.D: Desirable initiates DTP and auto accepts, yielding a trunk.

questions.question: A Cisco IP phone receives untagged data traffic from an attached PC. Which action is taken by the phone?

options.text: It allows the traffic to pass through unchanged.
It tags the traffic with the native VLAN.
It tags the traffic with the default VLAN.

questions.explanation: A Cisco IP phone typically acts as a small switch: untagged PC data frames traverse the phone toward the uplink unchanged, while voice can be tagged on the configured voice VLAN.

optionExplanations.A: Untagged PC data is normally forwarded, not discarded by the phone.
optionExplanations.B: The phone transparently forwards PC-originated untagged data onto the data VLAN.
optionExplanations.C: The phone does not universally insert a native-VLAN tag into untagged PC frames; native traffic is normally untagged.
optionExplanations.D: There is no requirement for the phone to tag PC data into a default VLAN.

questions.question: Which design element is a best practice when deploying an 802.11b wireless infrastructure?

options.text: allocating nonoverlapping channels to access points that are in close physical proximity to one another
disabling TCP so that access points can negotiate signal levels with their attached wireless devices
configuring access points to provide clients with a maximum of 5 Mbps
setting the maximum data rate to 54 Mbps on the Cisco Wireless LAN Controller

questions.explanation: Adjacent 802.11b APs should use nonoverlapping 2.4 GHz channels to reduce adjacent-channel interference; commonly channels 1, 6, and 11 in North America.

optionExplanations.A: Nonoverlapping nearby channels reduce adjacent-channel interference.
optionExplanations.B: TCP is an end-to-end transport protocol and is not disabled to negotiate radio signal levels.
optionExplanations.C: An arbitrary 5 Mbps client cap is not an 802.11b design requirement; 802.11b physical data rates go up to 11 Mbps.
optionExplanations.D: 54 Mbps is associated with 802.11g/a, not the maximum physical data rate of 802.11b.

questions.question: Which command should you enter to configure an LLDP delay time of 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: `lldp reinit 5` sets an LLDP reinitialization delay of five seconds using the supported command units.

optionExplanations.A: `lldp timer 5000` changes the advertisement interval to 5,000 seconds, not the reinit delay.
optionExplanations.B: `lldp holdtime 5` sets the advertised information retention time, not the reinit delay.
optionExplanations.C: `lldp reinit 5000` exceeds the accepted seconds range on standard Cisco platforms.
optionExplanations.D: `lldp reinit 5` configures the requested delay in seconds.

questions.question: How does STP prevent forwarding loops at OSI Layer 2?
questions.explanation: STP stops Layer 2 forwarding loops by placing redundant ports into a discarding/blocking role while preserving a loop-free forwarding tree.

optionExplanations.A: IP TTL limits routed packet lifetime; it is not STP’s loop-prevention mechanism.
optionExplanations.B: MAC address learning helps switches forward frames but does not prevent switching loops.
optionExplanations.C: Collision avoidance relates to media access, not blocking redundant Layer 2 paths.
optionExplanations.D: STP uses BPDU comparisons to prevent redundant ports from forwarding frames.

questions.question: Which type does a port become when it receives the best BPDU on a bridge?
questions.explanation: Each non-root bridge selects the root port based on the best received superior BPDU and cumulative path to the root bridge.

optionExplanations.A: Designated ports represent a LAN segment’s best advertised path toward the root; they are not chosen simply as the local port receiving the best BPDU.
optionExplanations.B: Backup ports are redundant ports providing an alternate to another port on the same shared segment.
optionExplanations.C: Alternate ports provide alternative paths but do not represent the selected best path.
optionExplanations.D: The root port is a non-root switch’s best path toward the root bridge, based on received BPDUs.

questions.question: Which value can you modify to configure a specific interface as the preferred forwarding interface?
questions.explanation: STP port priority is an adjustable component of the port ID; it can influence tie-breaking and which port is preferred in relevant STP elections.

optionExplanations.A: A physical interface number is not a tunable STP preference setting.
optionExplanations.B: Lower STP port priority can make a port more preferred when the preceding election criteria tie.
optionExplanations.C: VLAN or bridge priority primarily influences root-bridge election, not preference of a particular physical interface.
optionExplanations.D: Hello time is an STP timer; it is not the per-interface preference setting.

questions.question: Which statement about Cisco Discovery Protocol is true?

options.text: It runs on the network layer.
It can discover information from routers, firewalls, and switches.
It runs on the physical layer and the data link layer.

questions.explanation: CDP is Cisco proprietary and operates at Layer 2 to learn directly connected Cisco-neighbor information.

optionExplanations.A: CDP is a Cisco proprietary discovery protocol.
optionExplanations.B: CDP is a Layer 2 protocol, not a Layer 3 routing protocol.
optionExplanations.C: CDP may identify selected compatible device types, but this statement is broader and not its defining property across vendors/firewalls.
optionExplanations.D: CDP is not a protocol spanning both physical and data-link layers; it operates at Layer 2.

questions.question:
On a corporate network, hosts on the same VLAN can communicate with each other, but they are unable to communicate with hosts on different
VLANs. What is needed to allow communication between the VLANs?

options.text: a router with subinterfaces configured on the physical interface that is connected to the switch
a router with an IP address on the physical interface connected to the switch
a switch with an access link that is configured between the switches
a switch with a trunk link that is configured between the switches

questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing uses a trunk to an external router with 802.1Q-tagged subinterfaces, each with a gateway address for its VLAN.

optionExplanations.A: Router subinterfaces provide separate Layer 3 gateways and VLAN tagging on a single physical link.
optionExplanations.B: A single IP on one physical router interface cannot route multiple tagged VLANs without subinterface or equivalent configurations.
optionExplanations.C: An access link between switches alone does not route between VLAN IP subnets.
optionExplanations.D: A switch-to-switch trunk carries VLANs at Layer 2 but does not provide inter-VLAN Layer 3 routing.

questions.question: Which statement about LLDP is true?

options.text: It is a Cisco proprietary protocol.
It is configured in global configuration mode.
The LLDP update frequency is a fixed value.
It runs over the transport layer.

questions.explanation: LLDP has global configuration controls such as `lldp run` and `lldp timer`; individual ports may also have LLDP interface commands.

optionExplanations.A: LLDP is an IEEE standardized vendor-neutral discovery protocol, not Cisco proprietary CDP.
optionExplanations.B: LLDP includes global configuration commands for enabling and tuning advertisements.
optionExplanations.C: LLDP update rate is configurable, not permanently fixed.
optionExplanations.D: LLDP is a data-link discovery protocol, not a TCP/UDP transport-layer protocol.

questions.question: Which technology is used to improve web traffic performance by proxy caching?
questions.explanation: Cisco Web Security Appliance (WSA), now branded Cisco Secure Web Appliance, is the relevant web-proxy/security product that can provide proxy caching.

optionExplanations.A: WSA/Secure Web Appliance is Cisco’s secure web proxy platform and is capable of web content caching in supported deployments.
optionExplanations.B: Firepower is a network security/next-generation firewall platform, not specifically the web caching proxy answer.
optionExplanations.C: ASA is an adaptive security firewall platform, not primarily a proxy-cache solution.
optionExplanations.D: FireSIGHT is a security management/analytics product name, not a web caching proxy appliance.

questions.question: What criteria is used first during the root port selection process?

options.text: lowest path cost to the toot bridge

questions.explanation: STP root-port selection first compares cumulative root path cost for available candidate ports, then uses additional BPDU tie-breakers.

optionExplanations.A: Local port ID is used late in tie-breaking, not before root path cost.
optionExplanations.B: The path with lowest total cost toward the root is preferred before bridge/port-ID tie breakers.
optionExplanations.C: The sender or neighbor bridge ID can break equal-cost ties, but is not normally checked first.
optionExplanations.D: The sending port ID participates in later tie-breaking, not before path cost.

questions.question:
A network engineer must create a diagram of a multivendor network. Which command must be configured on the Cisco devices so that the
topology of the network is allowed to be mapped?
questions.explanation: `lldp run` enables vendor-neutral LLDP discovery globally so topology mapping can discover neighboring devices across multiple manufacturers.

optionExplanations.A: Global LLDP enables standards-based discovery for multi-vendor networks.
optionExplanations.B: `cdp run` enables Cisco proprietary CDP, not the preferred vendor-neutral discovery mechanism.
optionExplanations.C: `cdp enable` applies to a Cisco interface and remains proprietary.
optionExplanations.D: The suggested flow-sampler-map command is not a standard neighbor discovery command.

questions.question: How do AAA operations compare regarding user identification, user services, and access control?

options.text: Authorization provides access control, and authentication tracks user services
Authentication identifies users, and accounting tracks user services
Accounting tracks user services, and authentication provides access control
Authorization identifies users, and authentication provides access control

questions.explanation: AAA separates authentication (identifying/verifying identity), authorization (granting permitted actions), and accounting (recording sessions/usage).

optionExplanations.A: Authorization determines access privileges, while accounting—not authentication—tracks use of services.
optionExplanations.B: Authentication identifies/verifies users and accounting records their activity and service usage.
optionExplanations.C: Accounting logs activity; authentication alone does not determine all permitted actions.
optionExplanations.D: Authorization is permission control, not primarily identity verification, and authentication does not replace authorization.

questions.question: What is the difference between RADIUS and TACACS+?

options.text: RADIUS logs all commands that are entered by the administrator, but TACACS+ logs only start, stop, and interim commands.
TACACS+ separates authentication and authorization, and RADIUS merges them.
TACACS+ encrypts only password information, and RADIUS encrypts the entire payload.
RADIUS is most appropriate for dial authentication, but TACACS+ can be used for multiple types of authentication.

questions.explanation: TACACS+ supports separating authentication, authorization and accounting transactions, whereas RADIUS traditionally couples authorization attributes with authentication responses.

optionExplanations.A: RADIUS does not inherently provide TACACS+-style per-command accounting superiority; the statement reverses typical administrative capabilities.
optionExplanations.B: TACACS+ separates AAA processes, while RADIUS commonly combines authentication with authorization attributes.
optionExplanations.C: TACACS+ protects the packet body, while classic RADIUS primarily obfuscates passwords; the option reverses this.
optionExplanations.D: RADIUS supports multiple network-access contexts; this broad use-case distinction is not the protocol-defining contrast.

questions.question: How will Link Aggregation be implemented on a Cisco Wireless LAN Controller?

options.text: The EtherChannel must be configured in ג€mode activeג€.
When enabled, the WLC bandwidth drops to 500 Mbps.
To pass client traffic, two or more ports must be configured.
One functional physical port is needed to pass client traffic.

questions.explanation: AireOS Wireless LAN Controller link aggregation groups physical ports so member failures can be tolerated; a single working member can still forward traffic.

optionExplanations.A: WLC LAG configuration commonly uses static channel bundling rather than requiring LACP active negotiation.
optionExplanations.B: LAG aggregates available port capacity; it does not impose an intrinsic fixed 500 Mbps limit.
optionExplanations.C: Multiple ports improve bandwidth/redundancy but need not all be up for the bundle to carry traffic.
optionExplanations.D: A surviving functional LAG member can continue to carry controller client traffic.

questions.question: Which state does the switch port move to when PortFast is enabled?
questions.explanation: STP PortFast allows an eligible edge port to transition directly to forwarding on link-up without waiting through classic listening/learning states.

optionExplanations.A: Blocking prevents ordinary data forwarding; this is not the intended PortFast post-link state.
optionExplanations.B: Listening is normally bypassed when PortFast activates.
optionExplanations.C: Learning is also bypassed before immediate forwarding.
optionExplanations.D: Forwarding is the immediate functional PortFast edge-port state.

questions.question: Which protocol prompts the Wireless LAN Controller to generate its own local web administration SSL certificate for GUI access?
questions.explanation: HTTPS is the secure web-administration protocol and relies on a TLS certificate; older Cisco WLC material refers to this certificate as an SSL certificate.

optionExplanations.A: RADIUS is an AAA protocol for network access and does not enable the WLC secure web GUI.
optionExplanations.B: HTTPS uses TLS and a server certificate for the encrypted management interface.
optionExplanations.C: TACACS+ is an AAA protocol, not the browser’s encrypted GUI transport.
optionExplanations.D: HTTP lacks TLS encryption and certificate-based web server identity.

questions.question: An engineer must configure interswitch VLAN communication between a Cisco switch and a third-party switch. Which action should be taken?
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.1Q is the interoperable VLAN tagging standard used for trunk links between switches from different vendors.

optionExplanations.A: DSCP marks IP traffic quality of service and does not define VLAN trunk encapsulation.
optionExplanations.B: 802.1Q defines standardized Ethernet VLAN tags recognized across vendors.
optionExplanations.C: ISL is Cisco-proprietary legacy trunk encapsulation, not appropriate for multi-vendor interoperability.
optionExplanations.D: 802.1p specifies Layer 2 priority fields within 802.1Q tagging, not the overall VLAN trunk protocol.

questions.question: An engineer requires a switch interface to actively attempt to establish a trunk link with a neighbor switch. What command must be configured?
questions.explanation: Cisco DTP `dynamic desirable` mode actively transmits negotiation frames to attempt to form a trunk with a compatible neighbor.

optionExplanations.A: Static trunk mode forces trunk configuration and is not equivalent to actively negotiating DTP mode.
optionExplanations.B: Dynamic desirable actively initiates DTP trunk negotiation.
optionExplanations.C: Nonegotiate disables DTP frame exchange, contrary to actively attempting negotiation.
optionExplanations.D: Dynamic auto is passive and waits for a desirable or trunking peer to initiate.

questions.question: Which spanning-tree enhancement avoids the learning and listening states and immediately places ports in the forwarding state?
questions.explanation: PortFast bypasses conventional STP listening and learning states to put an edge port into forwarding immediately.

optionExplanations.A: BPDU filter affects BPDU transmission/reception behavior and is not the feature specifically defined by eliminating listener/learner delay.
optionExplanations.B: PortFast directly enters forwarding for the intended edge-port use.
optionExplanations.C: BackboneFast was a legacy convergence enhancement after indirect failures, not the immediate edge-port state transition.
optionExplanations.D: BPDU Guard err-disables a BPDU-receiving protected edge port; it does not accelerate forwarding.

questions.question: An engineer needs to add an old switch back into a network. To prevent the switch from corrupting the VLAN database, with action must be taken?

options.text: Add the switch in the VTP domain with a lower revision number.
Add the switch in the VTP domain with a higher revision number.
Add the switch with DTP set to dynamic desirable.
Add the switch with DTP set to desirable.

questions.explanation: VTP advertisements in VTPv1/v2 may overwrite VLAN state if a joining switch has a higher configuration revision. Verify and reset its revision before joining the domain.

optionExplanations.A: A lower revision number is the required safeguard for the legacy VTP risk, ideally resetting the joining device revision to zero before attaching it.
optionExplanations.B: A higher revision on a newly joined switch can override VLAN information and potentially remove existing VLANs.
optionExplanations.C: DTP dynamic desirable negotiates switch-port trunking, not the VLAN database revision or VTP propagation behavior.
optionExplanations.D: DTP desirable relates to trunk negotiation and cannot prevent a stale, high-revision VTP database from propagating.

questions.question:
An administrator must secure the WLC from receiving spoofed association requests. Which steps must be taken to configure the WLC to restrict
the requests and force the user to wait 10 ms to retry an association request?

options.text: Enable MAC filtering and set the SA Query timeout to 10.
Enable 802.1x Layer 2 security and set the Comeback timer to 10.
Enable Security Association Teardown Protection and set the SA Query timeout to 10.
Enable the Protected Management Frame service and set the Comeback timer to 10.

questions.explanation: IEEE 802.11w Protected Management Frames defends against spoofed association teardown. The association comeback timer controls how long a client waits before retrying; SA Query timeout is different.

optionExplanations.A: MAC filtering alone does not protect existing associations from spoofed reassociation/teardown requests, and SA Query timeout is not the comeback interval.
optionExplanations.B: 802.1X authenticates network access but its Layer 2 security setting does not by itself turn on the 802.11w association comeback mechanism.
optionExplanations.C: SA Query timeout controls how long to await an SA Query response; it is not the configured 10 ms retry delay.
optionExplanations.D: Enable PMF and configure the association comeback timer to 10 ms on the relevant supported AireOS controller; that timer governs retries after temporary rejection.

questions.question: An engineer must configure traffic for a VLAN that is untagged by the switch as it crosses a trunk link. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: On an 802.1Q trunk, the native VLAN carries untagged traffic by default; switchport trunk native vlan 10 sets VLAN 10 as native.

optionExplanations.A: Selecting 802.1Q encapsulation does not designate a VLAN to carry untagged frames.
optionExplanations.B: Allowing VLAN 10 across a trunk does not make VLAN 10 the native untagged VLAN.
optionExplanations.C: Trunk mode enables VLAN trunk forwarding but does not change the default native VLAN selection.
optionExplanations.D: Setting the trunk native VLAN to 10 assigns VLAN 10 as the VLAN for untagged frames received and, by default, sent on that trunk.

questions.question:
An engineer configures interface Gi1/0 on the company PE router to connect to an ISP. Neighbor discovery is disabled.
Which action is necessary to complete the configuration if the ISP uses third-party network devices?

options.text: Enable LLDP-MED on the ISP device.
Disable Cisco Discovery Protocol on the interface.

questions.explanation: LLDP is an open, multi-vendor Layer 2 neighbor discovery protocol. Enabling LLDP globally is necessary on Cisco devices when CDP cannot communicate with third-party peers.

optionExplanations.A: Autonegotiation concerns Ethernet speed/duplex, not vendor-neutral neighbor discovery advertisements.
optionExplanations.B: Enabling LLDP globally permits standards-based device discovery; also confirm that transmit/receive are enabled on the physical interface.
optionExplanations.C: LLDP-MED adds endpoint/device capabilities but is not generally necessary for router-to-ISP neighbor discovery.
optionExplanations.D: Disabling Cisco-proprietary CDP does not itself provide interoperable LLDP-based neighbor discovery.

questions.question: Which access point mode relies on a centralized controller for management, roaming, and SSID configuration?
questions.explanation: Lightweight access points are centrally managed using CAPWAP and a wireless LAN controller for SSID policy and roaming functions.

optionExplanations.A: Lightweight operation uses a WLC for central configuration and management rather than administering every AP independently.
optionExplanations.B: Autonomous APs are configured individually and do not require a WLC for WLAN operation.
optionExplanations.C: Bridge mode describes a wireless bridging role and does not itself imply centralized WLC dependence.
optionExplanations.D: Repeater mode extends radio coverage but does not define the central controller management model.

questions.question: Which access layer threat-mitigation technique provides security based on identity?
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.1X authenticates identities at the network access edge, with authorization decisions provided through an AAA/policy service.

optionExplanations.A: Dynamic ARP Inspection validates ARP messages against bindings and does not authenticate users or endpoint identities.
optionExplanations.B: DHCP snooping filters untrusted DHCP traffic and builds binding information, not identity-based admission.
optionExplanations.C: 802.1X is a port-based access-control mechanism using authentication via EAP and an AAA server.
optionExplanations.D: Using a nondefault native VLAN is a hardening practice but does not check a connecting user’s identity.

questions.question: Which interface mode must be configured to connect the lightweight APs in a centralized architecture?
questions.explanation: A centrally switched lightweight AP ordinarily attaches to a switch access port on its AP management VLAN; it tunnels WLAN client traffic to its WLC using CAPWAP.

optionExplanations.A: A WLC dynamic interface connects WLAN client VLANs on certain controllers; it is not the access-layer switch-port mode.
optionExplanations.B: A trunk might be required when a FlexConnect AP switches several VLANs locally, but is not intrinsically needed for standard centrally switched lightweight AP operation.
optionExplanations.C: An access port normally carries the AP’s management VLAN when client data is CAPWAP-tunneled to the controller.
optionExplanations.D: A management interface is a WLC logical interface, not a switch interface mode such as access or trunk.

questions.question: Which switching concept is used to create separate broadcast domains?
questions.explanation: A VLAN is a logical Layer 2 broadcast domain. Traffic between VLANs requires Layer 3 forwarding.

optionExplanations.A: Spanning Tree Protocol prevents forwarding loops within Layer 2 topologies; it does not partition networks into separate broadcast domains.
optionExplanations.B: VTP distributes VLAN configuration across participating switches, rather than itself defining the broadcast-domain boundary.
optionExplanations.C: VLANs logically separate Ethernet broadcast domains even when ports share the same physical switch infrastructure.
optionExplanations.D: CSMA/CD addresses medium access for half-duplex Ethernet and cannot provide broadcast-domain separation.

questions.question: What is a requirement when configuring or removing LAG on a WLC?

options.text: The incoming and outgoing ports for traffic flow must be specified if LAG is enabled.
The management interface must be reassigned if LAG is disabled
The controller must be rebooted after enabling or reconfiguring LAG
Multiple untagged interfaces on the same port must be supported

questions.explanation: On classic Cisco AireOS WLCs, changing LAG settings is committed by rebooting the controller, so the immediate reboot is recommended to finish the transition.

optionExplanations.A: AireOS LAG abstracts controller ports into one logical interface; you do not pin individual incoming/outgoing traffic flows to ports.
optionExplanations.B: Disabling LAG requires design review and can affect port/interface configuration, but management-interface reassignment is not a universal prerequisite.
optionExplanations.C: Enabling or changing the LAG mode requires a WLC reboot to complete the configuration change.
optionExplanations.D: LAG does not require supporting several untagged controller logical interfaces on one physical port.

questions.question: Which type of port is used to connect the wired network when an autonomous AP maps two VLANs to its WLANs?
questions.explanation: An autonomous AP supporting WLANs mapped to different wired VLANs typically uses an IEEE 802.1Q trunk to connect to the distribution switch.

optionExplanations.A: An access port carries one untagged access VLAN, so it cannot simultaneously transport two distinct WLAN VLANs as tagged traffic.
optionExplanations.B: A link aggregation group bundles physical links; it does not specify segregation of client VLANs on one link.
optionExplanations.C: A trunk carries 802.1Q-tagged frames for multiple mapped VLANs between AP and switch.
optionExplanations.D: EtherChannel aggregates links and need not carry multiple VLANs; it is not the required switch-port type here.

questions.question:
A network administrator needs to aggregate 4 ports into a single logical link which must negotiate layer 2 connectivity to ports on another switch.
What must be configured when using active mode on both sides of the connection?
questions.explanation: LACP allows two switches with compatible active-mode ports to negotiate a Layer 2 EtherChannel and operate four links as one logical bundle.

optionExplanations.A: LLDP discovers directly connected neighbor capabilities but does not negotiate Ethernet link aggregation.
optionExplanations.B: LACP is the standard EtherChannel negotiation protocol used by active/active peers.
optionExplanations.C: Cisco vPC lets a multi-chassis pair present a logical port-channel but is not the protocol negotiated by active-mode interfaces.
optionExplanations.D: 802.1Q provides tagged VLAN trunks; it does not itself dynamically aggregate four physical links.

questions.question:
An engineer is configuring data and voice services to pass through the same port. The designated switch interface fastethernet0/1 must transmit
packets using the same priority for data when they are received from the access port of the IP phone. Which configuration must be used?

options.text: interface fastethernet0/1 switchport voice vlan dot1p
interface fastethernet0/1 switchport priority extend cos 7
interface fastethernet0/1 switchport voice vlan untagged
interface fastethernet0/1 switchport priority extend trust

questions.explanation: The Cisco voice-VLAN priority extend trust setting tells an IP phone to preserve the CoS priority of data traffic from the attached PC rather than overwrite it.

optionExplanations.A: Voice VLAN dot1p controls 802.1p priority-tagged voice traffic handling, not preservation of data CoS from the PC-facing phone port.
optionExplanations.B: Priority extend cos 7 overwrites the PC traffic priority with CoS 7, not retain the incoming marking.
optionExplanations.C: Voice VLAN untagged configures handling of phone traffic without tagging; it does not preserve incoming data traffic priority.
optionExplanations.D: Priority extend trust permits the phone to retain the CoS value received from its attached data endpoint.

questions.question: Which port type supports the spanning-tree portfast command without additional configuration?
questions.explanation: Standard interface-level spanning-tree portfast applies to host-facing nontrunking/access switch ports. Trunk ports require the trunk form of the command where supported.

optionExplanations.A: A trunk needs explicit trunk-specific PortFast configuration in classic Cisco IOS; ordinary access-port command is not sufficient by default.
optionExplanations.B: Layer 3 subinterfaces route packets and are not STP switchports for this PortFast command.
optionExplanations.C: Layer 3 routed interfaces do not participate in Layer 2 STP in the same way as switch access ports.
optionExplanations.D: Access ports support the standard spanning-tree portfast interface command without the trunk keyword.

questions.question:
A Cisco engineer must configure a single switch interface to meet these requirements:
✑ Accept untagged frames and place them in VLAN 20
Accept tagged frames in VLAN 30 when CDP detects a Cisco IP phone
Which command set must the engineer apply?

options.text: switchport mode dynamic desirable switchport access vlan 20 switchport trunk allowed vlan 30 switchport voice vlan 30
switchport mode access switchport access vlan 20 switchport voice vlan 30
switchport mode dynamic auto switchport trunk native vlan 20 switchport trunk allowed vlan 30 switchport voice vlan 30
switchport mode trunk switchport access vlan 20 switchport voice vlan 30

questions.explanation: On a Cisco IP-phone switchport, an access VLAN carries untagged PC data while a distinct voice VLAN carries the tagged phone voice traffic.

optionExplanations.A: Dynamic desirable negotiation can create a trunk and adds unnecessary trunk commands; it does not implement the normal access-plus-voice port policy.
optionExplanations.B: Access VLAN 20 handles untagged data; voice VLAN 30 enables tagged frames sent by a CDP-capable Cisco IP phone.
optionExplanations.C: Dynamic auto and trunk-native configuration are inappropriate for the ordinary host-facing access-plus-voice configuration.
optionExplanations.D: A trunk interface is not the intended access-plus-voice configuration and switchport access vlan does not configure native VLAN on a trunk.

questions.question: What does a switch use to build its MAC address table?
questions.explanation: Ethernet switches learn MAC forwarding entries by examining the source MAC address of traffic arriving on an ingress port.

optionExplanations.A: VTP manages or distributes VLAN membership information; it does not build the table of source MAC-to-port mappings.
optionExplanations.B: DTP negotiates trunk links on supported Cisco switchports, rather than populate the MAC table.
optionExplanations.C: Ingress frames provide source MAC and ingress port information from which a switch creates dynamic CAM table entries.
optionExplanations.D: Egress traffic is already being forwarded and is not the primary source of new MAC-to-ingress-port learning.

questions.question:
What must a network administrator consider when deciding whether to configure a new wireless network with APs in autonomous mode or APs
running in cloud- based mode?

options.text: Autonomous mode APs are less dependent on an underlay but more complex to maintain than APs in cloud-based mode.
Cloud-based mode APs relay on underlays and are more complex to maintain than APs in autonomous mode.
Cloud-based mode APs are easy to deploy but harder to automate than APs in autonomous mode.
Autonomous mode APs are easy to deploy and automate than APs in cloud-based mode.

questions.explanation: Autonomous AP configuration is local and typically requires more per-AP maintenance; cloud-managed APs depend on cloud reachability for centralized management and automation.

optionExplanations.A: Autonomous APs are locally managed and less dependent on cloud management connectivity; fleet-wide changes are generally harder to maintain.
optionExplanations.B: Cloud management usually simplifies centralized rollout and operations rather than making them inherently more complex.
optionExplanations.C: Cloud platforms normally offer centralized policy and automation, so their automation is not inherently harder than autonomous AP automation.
optionExplanations.D: Autonomous deployments commonly require more manual per-AP work and are not inherently easier to automate at scale.

questions.question: What happens when a switch receives a frame with a destination MAC address that recently aged out?

options.text: The switch floods the frame to all ports in all VLANs except the port that received the frame.
The switch floods the frame to all ports in the VLAN except the port that received the frame.
The switch references the MAC address aging table for historical addresses on the port that received the frame.
The switch drops the frame and learns the destination MAC address again from the port that received the frame.

questions.explanation: When a dynamically learned destination MAC entry ages out, the destination becomes unknown and the switch floods that unicast frame to other forwarding ports in the same VLAN.

optionExplanations.A: Switches preserve VLAN boundaries and do not flood an unknown unicast across all VLANs.
optionExplanations.B: After the MAC-table entry expires, unknown-unicast flooding reaches other eligible forwarding ports in the original VLAN.
optionExplanations.C: Forwarding decisions use the current MAC address table; no universal historic aging table is consulted for this destination.
optionExplanations.D: Switches can learn a source address from ingress frames, but do not learn an unknown destination by simply dropping the frame.

questions.question: What is a function of store-and forward switching?

options.text: It reduces latency by eliminating error checking within the frame
It produces an effective level of error-free network traffic using CRCs.
It buffers frames and forwards regardless of errors within the frames.
It forwards a frame by checking only the destination MAC address

questions.explanation: Store-and-forward switching receives the full Ethernet frame and checks its FCS/CRC before forwarding, reducing propagation of corrupted frames.
